chart_data_needs.title: Quantum Computing Market Size Forecast (2022-2030)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: How large is the total addressable market for quantum computing, and what is the projected growth trajectory through 2030?
required_metrics: Source: Gartner, IDC, McKinsey, BCG, or similar
comparison_set: Annual market size estimates from multiple analyst firms (e.g., Gartner, IDC, Fortune Business Insights) to show consensus range.
search_queries: quantum computing market size CAGR 2022-2030 report
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use only published reports from recognized analyst firms. If only two endpoints are available, mark intermediate years as estimates based on CAGR from the source.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Establishes the market opportunity size and growth rate to justify investment interest.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: Before showing the market size, the report argues that quantum computing is transitioning from research to commercial viability, and executives need to understand the scale of the opportunity.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: The quantum computing market is projected to grow from $X billion in 2022 to $Y billion by 2030, representing a CAGR of Z%, indicating a rapidly expanding market that warrants strategic attention.

chart_data_needs.title: Annual Quantum Computing Patent Filings by Top Companies (2022-2026)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: Which companies are leading in quantum IP creation, and how has the patent landscape evolved?
required_metrics: Number of patents granted or filed
Company: IBM, Google, IonQ, NexusQuantum, Rigetti, others
comparison_set: Year-over-year patent counts for each major company.
search_queries: quantum computing patents by company 2022 2023 2024 2025 2026 USPTO
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use patent grant or publication year. If exact annual data is unavailable, use filing year and note the lag.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Demonstrates competitive intensity and innovation leadership among key players.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: The report claims that hardware and software innovation is accelerating, and patent filings are a leading indicator of R&D investment.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: IBM, Google, and NexusQuantum have filed the most patents in 2026, with a significant increase from 2022, signaling a race to secure intellectual property.

chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Shows investor confidence and identifies hot sub-sectors.

chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Hardware startups raised $X billion in 2026, up Y% from 2025, while software startups saw a Z% increase, indicating balanced growth across the stack.

chart_data_needs.title: Quantum Processor Fidelity Comparison (2026)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: How do leading quantum processors compare in terms of qubit count, fidelity, and commercial availability?
required_metrics: Processor name (e.g., NexusQuantum 500, IBM Eagle, Google Sycamore, IonQ Aria)
comparison_set: All major quantum processors announced or available in 2026.
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use only officially reported fidelity metrics. If not available, mark as 'not disclosed'.

chart_data_needs.title: Adoption of Quantum Computing in Financial Services (2024-2026)

required_metrics: Number of financial institutions using quantum computing for risk/optimization

search_queries: quantum computing adoption financial services 2024 2025 2026 survey
banks using quantum computing risk management 2026
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use only publicly announced deployments or survey results with clear methodology.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Provides evidence of real-world adoption in a key vertical.

chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: By 2026, over 20 financial institutions have deployed quantum-based risk models, up from 5 in 2024, indicating accelerating adoption.

chart_data_needs.title: Quantum Computing Energy Consumption Trends (2024-2026)
chart_data_needs.executive_question: How does the energy consumption of quantum cooling systems compare to classical HPC, and is it improving?
required_metrics: Energy consumption per qubit (kW/qubit) or total system power (kW)
System type: Quantum (dilution refrigerator) vs Classical HPC (per FLOP)
comparison_set: Year-over-year energy consumption for quantum systems and classical HPC.
chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Use published benchmarks from reputable sources. If exact data is unavailable, use estimates from DOE or IEA and note as such.
chart_data_needs.narrative_role: Addresses the challenge of power consumption as a barrier to adoption.
chart_data_needs.pre_exhibit_context: The report notes that high power consumption for cooling remains a challenge; this chart quantifies the issue.
chart_data_needs.post_exhibit_takeaway: Quantum cooling systems consume 10x more energy per qubit than classical HPC per operation, but efficiency improved by 15% from 2024 to 2026.

chart_data_needs.data_quality_rule: Include only events with confirmed dates from credible sources. Use month precision where possible.
